The runtime spread is unprotected even though &#39;id&#39; and &#39;layoutId&#39; are omitted from the types.src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx: &lt;motion.div {...entityProps(entity,&#39;box&#39;)} {...rest} style=...&gt; | src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx: {...entityProps(entity,&#39;arrow&#39;)} {...rest} | src/presentation-kit/nodes/geometry.ts entityProps returns layoutId, data-presentation-&lt;hook&gt; and data-presentation-entity | judging basis: consensus-fail | src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx | src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx | src/presentation-kit/nodes/geometry.ts
engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passPass: none of the delivered browser tests sleeps for a fixed time before asserting. Each one waits for observable state. Which tests drive a browser: vitest.config.ts runs tests/unit only, under jsdom. vitest.integration.config.ts runs tests/integration and tests/e2e under node. Only those two folders contain browser tests. The only test that drives Playwright itself is in tests/integration/inspect.test.ts; it launches chromium at line 125. In tests/unit/scripts.test.ts, captureSteps gets a plain mock object whose waitForTimeout only records an event, so no browser runs there. The one test that drives a page directly is &#39;removes the exiting scene host…&#39; (inspect.test.ts:252-265). It calls page.waitForSelector(&#39;[data-step-count]&#39;), presses ArrowRight, then polls with page.waitForFunction until the scene-host count is 1, with a 5000 ms timeout. Only after that wait does it read locator.count(), and it uses that count purely as an assertion, not as a wait. Every other browser test starts the inspect or verify scripts as child processes through run() (support.ts:48-56). run() resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, so each test waits for the process to finish before checking its exit code, output, or files. This covers the INT-002 helper tests, the bootstrap tests, and the e2e verify tests. None of the quoted test files calls waitForTimeout, setTimeout, or any other sleep while waiting. The setTimeout calls in the inspect fixture (line 53) and in the verify-failures fault edits (lines 73-91) are code written into the app under test, not waits in the test. Panel A and panel B: their reasons match the cited code, so I rule their pass. Panel C: C fails the &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39; test (inspect.test.ts:222-250) because it passes --settle 1200 and --settle 50. That reason does not decide this criterion. Those flags set the delivered helper&#39;s own settle interval; they are the feature the test is checking, not a sleep the test uses to wait for a transition before asserting. The test itself waits for each child process to close (run() → &#39;close&#39;). It then makes deterministic assertions on the screenshot pixels and on the capture-log timing (capturedAt − navigatedAt ≥ 1200). skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:196 Entry-file replacement: the `apply` function writes the replacement entry with `cpSync(..., TEMPLATES.bootstrap/src/main.tsx)` in the files loop, but only if `exists && !isEntry` is false. If the original entry is `src/main.tsx` and it is backed up, fine. However, when the entry is a different file (e.g. `src/index.tsx`), `src/main.tsx` may already exist as unrelated user code. The host and `TalkScene` therefore stay mounted and receive only a new payload `n`, instead of remounting. Identity: `entities.ts` defines the presentation-owned `E` ids, such as `hmp/card-${i}`, and `TalkScene` passes them as `entity=` on every Box, Arrow, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame. Each of those components spreads `entityProps(entity, hook)`, which sets `layout: true` and `layoutId: entity`. Stage wraps everything in `LayoutGroup`. tiebreaks{"demo-integration":null,"scene-kit":null,"presentation-skill":null,"verification-tooling":{"ok":true,"criteria":["verification-step-error-fails"],"inventory_kind":"neutral source","attempts":[{"stage":"tiebreak","attempt":1,"ok":true,"error":null}],"first_results":[{"id":"verification-step-error-fails","verdict":"fail","rationale":"I&#39;m ruling with Judge B. The verifier fails real render and transition faults, and the e2e regressions for them exist: &#39;render fault that breaks step 6&#39; and &#39;transition that does not advance the step index&#39;. However, the review guidance says to fail when the transition check turns a non-numeric hook into a number that still satisfies its comparison, and gives the first step as the example. In scripts/verify.mjs, waitForIndex maps only a null attribute to null and passes every other raw string through Number(raw). An empty or whitespace data-step-index (&#39;&#39; or &#39; &#39;) becomes 0, so actual === expected holds when i === 0. The loop in renderSample then treats step 1 as reached, even though the hook is non-numeric. The requirement that a missing or non-numeric hook is never counted as progress is therefore unmet. Judges A and C point to indexProblem rejecting null and NaN, and to !(count &gt; 0) guarding the step count. Both observations are accurate, but neither decides the criterion. indexProblem runs only when waitForIndex has not already returned, and an empty string never becomes NaN or null: it becomes 0 and returns early at the equality check. The &#39;removes the exiting scene host&#39; test does wait on state: it uses waitForSelector and a waitForFunction poll with a timeout, and its count() comes after that wait and serves only as an assertion. The &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39; test waits for the subprocess to exit through run() in support.ts:48-56, which resolves on &#39;close&#39;. The waitForTimeout(settleMs) at inspect-presentation.mjs:176 belongs to the shipped helper&#39;s settle feature, not to the test. Those two tests look acceptable. But the ruling itself says the browser-driving tests live in tests/integration and tests/e2e, and the claim that &#39;every other browser test&#39; runs scripts through run() and that &#39;none of these tests calls waitForTimeout&#39; is not backed by any quoted line. No other part of inspect.test.ts is quoted, and nothing from verify-failures.test.ts or any tests/e2e file is quoted. The material is complete and in scope (no truncation or omission marker), but it does not establish the universal no-fixed-sleep condition. The quoted lines support the claim for the parts they show. In the cross-group test (inspect.test.ts:252-265), page.waitForSelector and a page.waitForFunction poll with a timeout come before locator.count(), and count() is only asserted, not used as a wait. The subprocess tests await run(), which resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (support.ts:48-56).
